findings.description: A normal `.readerMode` tap dispatches `showReaderMode`, but this reducer now sets `.readerModeLongPressAction`. The display handler maps that state to `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()`, which adds the current page to the reading list, instead of `toggleReaderMode()`. findings.failureMode: On a reader-capable page, tap the Reader Mode toolbar button; the page is added to Reading List instead of entering reader mode.

findings.description: `.available` means this tap will enable reader mode, while `.active` means it will disable it, so these changed branches compute the opposite post-tap state. In the current telemetry helper that value lands in `is_private`; consequently the unchanged reader-button test now gets `true` rather than its expected `false` from the default `nil` state, and a normal active reader page is falsely reported as private when closed. Restore `true` for `.available` and `false` otherwise.
findings.failureMode: Run `testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes`, or tap Reader Mode on an active normal tab; the telemetry extra is wrong and the existing unit test fails.
findings.title: Restore the post-tap reader-mode telemetry state

findings.description: Reader-mode URLs use the HTTP `localhost/reader-mode/page` form, so `isWebPage()` is already true for them. This new `||` therefore forwards the raw internal reader URL in the cancel action; `handleCancelEditAction` replaces the address-bar URL with it, and `LocationView` renders that URL's `absoluteString`. After editing the address on a reader-mode page and cancelling (or opening tabs/menu, which also calls this helper), the bar shows the internal localhost URL instead of the decoded article URL. Restore the reader-mode exclusion with `currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL`.
findings.failureMode: Enter reader mode, start editing the address, then cancel; the address bar changes from the article URL to Firefox's internal localhost reader URL.
findings.title: Keep the internal reader URL out of the address bar

findings.description: The emitted controller retains `require("@calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService")`, but that installed subpath contains only TypeScript and Node cannot resolve it; the Nest build emits no feature-service JS. findings.description: The endpoint declares `TEAM_MEMBER`, and `RolesGuard` uses the ordered role list plus `checkedRoleIndex <= requiredRoleIndex`; an ordinary MEMBER therefore satisfies this threshold. Since the handler immediately mints an invite with no subsequent permission check, the added non-admin E2E case deterministically receives 200 instead of its required 403. Use `TEAM_ADMIN`.

findings.title: Require the team-admin role for invite creation

findings.description: The created row stores the random invite secret in `token` and a predictable label such as `invite-link-for-teamId-42` in `identifier`, but this return value now exposes the label as `data.token`. findings.failureMode: Any successful create-invite call returns a predictable identifier in the token field while the URL contains a different secret; repeated calls return the same token value and consumers cannot redeem it.
findings.title: Return the generated token, not its identifier

findings.description: Changing `if (!isOrgContext)` to `if (isOrgContext)` swaps the established destinations for both contexts: organization/sub-team invites now go to `/teams`, while standalone-team invites go through organization signup/onboarding. The `/teams` page is the code path that actually consumes a normal team token, and this shared service also backs existing TRPC and organization API callers. Restore the negation so standalone teams use `/teams` and organization contexts use `/signup` with the onboarding callback.
findings.failureMode: Creating any invite returns a URL for the opposite context; regular-team recipients are sent into organization signup/onboarding, while organization recipients are sent to the standalone teams flow.

findings.description: This added spec is placed under the API-v2 spec exclusion, and an explicit Vitest run against it exits successfully with “No test files found”; the file is instead matched by API v2's Jest E2E configuration. findings.description: The DTO says every returned link opens `/signup`, but this endpoint accepts standalone teams as well as organization contexts and `TeamService` has separate `/teams` and `/signup` branches. findings.description: Every `showReaderMode` action now emits `.readerModeLongPressAction`; `BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions` handles that by creating a Reading List record instead of calling `toggleReaderMode()`. This breaks the normal reader-mode toolbar tap, the accessibility Magic Tap, and the summarizer long-press fallback, all of which dispatch `showReaderMode`: they add the page to Reading List and never toggle reader mode. Restore `.readerMode` in `handleShowReaderModeAction`; the distinct `addToReadingListLongPressAction` reducer already handles the long-press behavior.

findings.title: Reader-mode taps are routed to the long-press action

findings.description: Reader pages use an internal `http://localhost/reader-mode/page` URL, while normal URL-bar updates deliberately store `tab.url?.displayURL` so the original article URL is shown. Because `isReaderModeURL` also satisfies `isWebPage()`, the new `||` preserves the raw internal URL and the cancel action replaces the display URL with it. While viewing reader mode, tapping Cancel, Tabs, or Menu (all call this helper) therefore leaves the address bar showing the localhost reader endpoint. Keep reader-mode URLs excluded (the prior `&& !currentURL.isReaderModeURL`) or pass their decoded display URL.
findings.failureMode: Open reader mode, enter URL editing, then cancel or tap Menu/Tabs; the toolbar shows the internal localhost reader-mode URL rather than the article URL.
findings.title: Canceling edit exposes the internal reader URL

findings.description: For `.available`, tapping the button opens reader mode, while tapping from `.active` closes it, so the prior mapping (`available -> true`, otherwise `false`) matched the post-tap `enabled` meaning in `toolbar.yaml`. This inversion supplies the opposite state. Because the existing telemetry helper forwards `isEnabled` into the `isPrivate` extra, it also makes the unchanged reader-mode middleware test fail: its default nil state now yields `isEnabled = true`, so `savedExtras.isPrivate` is true instead of the asserted false. findings.description: The iOS paste permission alert is presented asynchronously, but this only waits 0.5 seconds for existence and then taps without checking hittability. On a loaded simulator where “Allow Paste” appears late—or exists while its presentation animation still makes it non-hittable—this call misses/fails to tap it; the alert blocks the paste and `mozWaitForValueContains` times out for every caller. Existing paste-alert handling waits for the alert button to become hittable with `TIMEOUT`; use similarly robust synchronization while still treating an already-granted prompt as optional.
findings.failureMode: On iOS 16+ with paste permission undecided and SpringBoard presenting or animating the system alert outside the 0.5-second existence window, the helper does not accept the alert and fails its URL assertion.

findings.description: The `<=` loop executes once past `keys_result->numkeys`. For an ordinary one-key command the extra zero-initialized `keysbuf` entry points at `argv[0]`, so the command name is hashed as a second key and most valid GET/SET requests are rejected as CROSSSLOT; it also writes `slot_buffer[numkeys]` beyond the allocation, and larger dynamically allocated key arrays can be read out of bounds, making a client command capable of corrupting memory or crashing the server. Use `j < keys_result->numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: In cluster mode, preprocess a valid one-key command such as `GET foo`; the loop hashes `foo`, then hashes `GET` from the non-key entry and performs a heap out-of-bounds write, yielding a spurious CROSSSLOT error and potential process crash.
findings.title: Stop slot extraction before the end of the key array

Every HINCRBYFLOAT then sends a malformed command to replicas and writes it to AOF; the new replication assertion cannot match it, replicas reject it, and AOF replay cannot restore the update. Change the count to 7.

For `HSETEX h EX ...` followed by `HINCRBYFLOAT h f ...`, HPTTL now returns -1 instead of the remaining TTL, and the existing `HINCRBYFLOAT - preserve expiration time of the field` test fails. The rewritten HSETEX only affects propagation/AOF; it does not repair the primary write, and it can leave the replica retaining a TTL that the primary removed. Keep HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL on this hashTypeSet call.
findings.failureMode: An ordinary HINCRBYFLOAT against a field with a TTL removes the primary's expiration and creates primary/replica TTL divergence.
findings.title: Preserve the field TTL on the primary update

findings.description: This replacement escapes LIKE metacharacters on the raw keyword but drops the prior `unicode_escape` conversion. `WorkflowRun.inputs` and `outputs` are `LongText` populated using default `json.dumps`, so an account-created run containing (for example) `中文` stores `\u4e2d\u6587`; the new `%中文%` pattern returns no log even though the value is present. Keep the JSON-compatible Unicode conversion, then apply `escape_like_pattern` before building the LIKE value.

findings.title: Retain JSON encoding for workflow-log Unicode search

findings.description: The helper prefixes `%`, `_`, and `\` with a backslash, but this SQL declares `|` as the escape character. With `IRIS_TEXT_INDEX` disabled, a query such as `50%` is bound as `%50\%%`; IRIS treats that backslash literally and the following `%` as a wildcard, so literal-percent searches either miss the matching document or admit wildcard matches. Declare backslash as the SQL escape character, or escape the pattern with `|`.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback full-text search gives wrong results for query text containing LIKE metacharacters.
findings.title: Use the same escape character in the IRIS LIKE clause

findings.description: The replacement vector supplies seven objects (`HSETEX`, key, `KEEPTTL`, `FIELDS`, count, field, value) but declares `argc` as 6. `rewriteClientCommandVector` reads only that many varargs, so `newobj` is omitted and replicas/AOF receive `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field` without a value. In execution, the replica reported a wrong-arity HSETEX and retained value `1` while the master became `2.1`; pass 7 as the vector length.

findings.description: For an existing hash field with an expiration, this call omits `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL`. `hashTypeSet` interprets that omission by persisting the field, so `HINCRBYFLOAT` immediately changes the master's HTTL to -1 instead of retaining the deadline. This breaks the command's existing TTL-preservation contract (and the pre-existing test at line 851); keep `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` on the local update independently of the propagation rewrite.
findings.failureMode: Run HSET/HPEXPIRE and then HINCRBYFLOAT on the expiring field. On the reviewed binary HPTTL changed from 99997 to -1, so the field no longer expires.
findings.title: HINCRBYFLOAT now clears the master's field TTL

findings.description: The inclusive loop processes index `numkeys` after the last key and writes `slot_buffer[numkeys]` past the allocation. For an ordinary one-key cluster command, the extra `keysbuf` entry is typically zero, so this also hashes `argv[0]` and usually misclassifies the command as cross-slot; with heap-backed key results it can read an uninitialized/out-of-bounds position and crash or corrupt memory. Restore the strict `< keys_result->numkeys` bound.
findings.failureMode: Any keyed command reaches an extra iteration; it performs a heap out-of-bounds write and may reject a valid request, access an invalid argv element, or crash.
findings.title: Stop slot extraction before `numkeys`

This branch is patch 1 while the checked-in package baseline is still 9.0.0, so `== '1'` runs BUILD002 against the stale major-version baseline and can reject legitimate 10.0 dependency changes; once the branch advances to patch 2, it disables the servicing restriction entirely and lets dependency removals through. The first-patch exception must be `!= '1'`, so patch 1 skips the stale check and subsequent servicing patches enforce it.
findings.failureMode: On the current 10.0.1 build, any dependency present in the stale 9.0 baseline but legitimately removed by 10.0 makes `UnusedBaselinePackageReference` nonempty and fails BUILD002; after incrementing to 10.0.2, the same wrong predicate instead suppresses BUILD002 and permits breaking package dependency removal.
findings.title: Fix the inverted first-servicing-patch gate

findings.description: The checked-in servicing manifest still assigns the pre-RTM placeholder `10.0.25.52413` to the managed framework files, while both the released `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref` 10.0.0 manifest and actual 10.0.0 runtime binary report `10.0.25.52411`. This manifest feeds SDK conflict resolution, which compares file versions to choose a winner; overstating the platform version can make an application package assembly with an intermediate/newer real version lose to the older shared-framework assembly. Copy the released 10.0.0 `data/PlatformManifest.txt` values for all affected entries.
findings.failureMode: When a referenced package contributes one of these assemblies at the same assembly version with a file version newer than the actual 10.0.0 shared-framework file but below the claimed 10.0.25.52413, ResolvePackageFileConflicts treats the platform as newer and removes the package asset, so the published app runs the older framework binary.
findings.title: Replace the pre-RTM placeholder file versions

findings.description: The new call relies on `AddPackageSource`, whose whole-file grep treats a commented `dotnet-eng-internal` entry as already active (the same applies to dotnet-tools). With an active public source and an old internal entry retained in a comment, the script exits successfully without adding any usable internal source, so restores that need an internal package fail. Make the new path use active XML nodes rather than the grep-based helper result.
findings.failureMode: Run the script on a config with an active dotnet-eng source and a commented-out dotnet-eng-internal entry; it prints that the internal source is enabled but leaves zero active entries, and a build needing an internal-only package fails restore.
findings.title: Do not let commented internal feeds satisfy the add operation

findings.description: The branch now sets `PreReleaseVersionLabel` to `servicing`, but the replacement conditional mapping only handles alpha, preview, rc, and rtm. Therefore `PreReleaseBrandingLabel` is empty on every non-stabilized servicing build, and `PackageBrandingVersion` is emitted as `10.0.1 Build ...` instead of identifying it as a Servicing build. Add the corresponding `servicing` mapping (for example `Servicing`).
findings.failureMode: For any normal servicing build with a nonempty VersionSuffix, `Directory.Build.targets` constructs installer/package display branding from an unset `PreReleaseBrandingLabel`, producing metadata that omits the servicing designation.
findings.title: Define branding for the new servicing label

findings.description: The new Unix checks grep the entire XML text instead of querying the `packageSources` element as the PowerShell implementation does. A valid config where `<add key="dotnet-eng" ...>` or `dotnet-tools` appears only inside a comment is therefore rewritten to include the corresponding internal feed even though no active trigger source exists. Restrict both checks to active XML nodes under `packageSources`; otherwise the script produces a NuGet.config with an unintended package source.
findings.failureMode: Run SetupNugetSources.sh on a valid config where dotnet-eng or dotnet-tools appears only in an XML comment; the script reports it as present and inserts a live `-internal` package source instead of leaving the config unchanged.
findings.title: Do not treat commented feed entries as active sources

findings.description: This replacement escapes LIKE metacharacters on the raw keyword but drops the prior `unicode_escape` conversion. `WorkflowRun.inputs` and `outputs` are `LongText` populated using default `json.dumps`, so an account-created run containing (for example) `中文` stores `\u4e2d\u6587`; the new `%中文%` pattern returns no log even though the value is present. Keep the JSON-compatible Unicode conversion, then apply `escape_like_pattern` before building the LIKE value.
findings.failureMode: Workflow log keyword search omits runs whose JSON inputs or outputs contain non-ASCII text.
findings.title: Retain JSON encoding for workflow-log Unicode search

findings.description: The helper prefixes `%`, `_`, and `\` with a backslash, but this SQL declares `|` as the escape character. With `IRIS_TEXT_INDEX` disabled, a query such as `50%` is bound as `%50\%%`; IRIS treats that backslash literally and the following `%` as a wildcard, so literal-percent searches either miss the matching document or admit wildcard matches. Declare backslash as the SQL escape character, or escape the pattern with `|`.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback full-text search gives wrong results for query text containing LIKE metacharacters.
findings.title: Use the same escape character in the IRIS LIKE clause

findings.description: When the executor returns no `result` key or `result=None`, this condition skips validation and returns `None` despite the declared `str` contract. Both required static checkers reject line 40 (`str | None` is not assignable to `str`); if run, `TemplateTransformNode._run()` also calls `len(None)` and crashes instead of returning a failed result. Reject every non-string result with `TemplateRenderError`.
findings.failureMode: The changed production code fails strict type checking unconditionally, and a missing/null executor result reaches `len(None)` and crashes template-transform execution.
findings.title: Reject `None` render results

findings.description: The factory has already resolved `node_class` from the requested version, but this new branch unconditionally constructs `TemplateTransformNode`. If another template-transform version is registered and a workflow requests it, the factory now silently executes v1 behavior instead of the selected implementation; before this branch, `return node_class(...)` honored that version. Limit the injected-renderer branch to the concrete class that supports it or instantiate the resolved class while preserving its contract.
findings.failureMode: A workflow whose template-transform node requests a registered non-v1 version is created as the v1 `TemplateTransformNode`, producing the wrong version's output on execution.
findings.title: Do not bypass the version-resolved template node class

findings.description: The optional parameter's absent value is `None`, but this `or` treats a valid falsey renderer as absent. The factory therefore replaces it with a `CodeExecutor` adapter before creating template nodes, causing those nodes to run the sandbox-backed renderer instead of the injected implementation. Use an explicit `is not None` check.
findings.failureMode: A valid falsey renderer injected into `DifyNodeFactory` is replaced, so every template-transform node created by that factory executes the wrong renderer.
findings.title: Preserve falsey renderers passed to the factory

findings.description: The parameter uses `None` to mean “not supplied”, but `template_renderer or ...` also discards any valid renderer instance whose `__bool__` is false. Directly constructing the node with such a renderer unexpectedly invokes the real `CodeExecutor` adapter, which can produce different output or contact the sandbox instead of the injected renderer. Select the default only with `template_renderer is None`.
findings.failureMode: A valid falsey renderer injected into `TemplateTransformNode` is ignored, so `_run` executes the sandbox-backed renderer rather than the caller's implementation.
findings.title: Preserve falsey renderers passed directly to the node

findings.failureMode: Running the mandatory Ruff format check on the changed Python files fails because this function signature would be reformatted.

Both required production type-checkers reject this changed return (`str | None` is not assignable to `str`); at runtime the caller also reaches `len(None)` instead of a `TemplateRenderError`. Raise `TemplateRenderError` when the key is absent/null before returning.

For example, supplying such a test or stateful renderer causes the factory to call the sandbox-backed renderer and return its output instead. Use an explicit `is not None` check here and in `TemplateTransformNode` line 41.

findings.title: Do not discard valid falsy renderer injections
